page: Microsoft Azure B2ats_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Basv2 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This server features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The hardware profile includes a tiny memory allocation of 1.0 GB RAM, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.5 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2701.19 in stress-ng tests, which places it in the top 25%. However, its multi-core performance is weak, scoring the same 2701.19 in stress-ng multi-core tests, placing it in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is highly constrained, with a cached read-only small block memory bandwidth of 140.76 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 0.0, both ranking in the bottom 10%. PassMark CPU testing yields a weak score of 3130.58, with poor results in physics and extended instructions.

The primary tradeoff of the B2ats_v2 is its extremely limited memory capacity of 1.0 GB paired with a burstable CPU allocation model. This makes it highly cost-efficient for low-intensity, intermittent workloads but unsuitable for memory-heavy or sustained multi-threaded processing. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform poorly, with Redis achieving 2.25 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is also limited to 2.77 GB/sec. Consequently, this server is best suited for lightweight, burstable applications, simple microservices, development environments, or low-traffic web serving where resource demands are minimal and cost minimization is prioritized.
